newsitem.title: USA: Saf T Lok trade heavy after handgun rules.
newsitem.headline: Saf T Lok trade heavy after handgun rules.

text.p: Gun safety lock maker Saf T Lok Inc was heavily traded on Thursday in a surge caused by new presidential handgun rules, traders said.

Shares in the Tequesta, Fla., company were off 1/2 at 4-1/2 in midafternoon, falling from a morning surge that took the price to 6-3/4. Volume was 704,000 shares, more than 50 times normal daily activity.
"My instinct is that with the President signing an executive order to mandate locks on all handguns, people are figuring they are in line for some business," a trader said.

He and other traders called the activity a follow-through from President Bill Clinton's order on Wednesday requiring personnel at federal law enforcement agencies to put child safety locks on their weapons. The move was part of a package of restrictions on gun buyers.
The shares leaped after Clinton's announcement Wednesday afternoon, closing up about 2-3/4 to five. The shares rose on Thursday to an intraday high of 6-3/4 before slipping.
Saf T Lok also makes personal computer-based editing systems.
